complexity.correctness_note: NeetCode accepts this, so its driver does construct nodes from the submission's own TreeNode — verified by acceptance, and locally by running the solution both ways: with this file's TreeNode it returns [[1],[2,3],[4,5,7]]; with a plain TreeNode it raises AttributeError. K3 had assumed the judge supplies its own class, which is how LeetCode's driver behaves but not this one.
complexity.correctness_reason: Depends on the judge building nodes from the TreeNode class this file defines: the solution redefines TreeNode with a `children` property and reads node.children. Handed a node built from the problem's own commented definition instead, it raises AttributeError.
complexity.notes: The custom set2 dedup is unnecessary (a tree node has exactly one parent, so duplicates never occur), and TreeNode.__iter__/__next__ are dead code that also violate the iterator protocol. A collections.deque with popleft() would restore the standard O(n) BFS. The local TreeNode redefinition adds a `children` property that the harness-supplied nodes do not have.
complexity.summary: Iterative BFS that processes one frontier list per level, collecting children into a custom dedup wrapper (set2) for the next level. Using list.pop(0) to drain each frontier costs O(L) per pop, so each level of width L costs O(L^2) and the whole traversal degrades to O(n^2) on bushy trees.
